answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a refundable identity bond plus peer attestation: each identity locks a small deposit at a public wharf of registration, and every action it takes must be countersigned by peers who stake their own reputation. At dawn of each epoch, honest identities earn their bond back with interest, while a Sybil operator spawning thousands of fakes must fund every bond and keep each one behaving well. The cost scales linearly with fake identities, like filling an ocean one cup at a time, while honest agents pay almost nothing.
